item.title: Holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial says he "didn't have any doubts"
item.description: Michael Desronvil, the lone holdout juror in the high-profile Lindsay Clancy murder trial, said he "didn't have any doubts" during deliberations.

item.title: Mountain lion runs wild on streets of San Francisco
item.description: A chase for a wild mountain lion terrorizing locals on the streets of San Francisco ended with the feline being caught and carried to safety. Carter Evans has the story.

item.title: Princess Diana's brother makes "astonishing claims" against King Charles in new book
item.description: The late Princess Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, is making astonishing claims related to his sister's death and King Charles' behavior at the time in a new book. Holly Williams has more.

item.title: Holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy case says he "didn't have any doubts" about her guilt
item.description: The holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy's triple murder case has released a statement. Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Watch: Images show damage to plane after power bank bursts into flames during flight
item.description: A power bank overheated and caught fire on a flight from Amsterdam to Curacao on Friday, charring part of the plane. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: Most Americans think AI will harm humans, CBS News polling shows
item.description: Amid growing warnings about the pace of AI development, Americans told CBS News what they think of the tech. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto reports.

item.title: Details on Trump's announced White House ban against CNN, MS NOW and Politico
item.description: President Trump on Friday announced he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. CBS News' Natalie Brand reports.

item.title: Trump says he's struck deal for "permanent control over security" in Greenland
item.description: President Trump said he struck a deal to give the United States "permanent control over security ... in Greenland," following a push by the president to boost the U.S.' influence over the island — or take it over.

item.title: Nvidia CEO calls for AI to be developed "as fast as we can"
item.description: The CEO of the world's largest chipmaker told CBS News that tech companies should proceed with artificial intelligence development despite recent warnings from worried industry leaders that there may be a need to pull back.

item.title: Trump says he's banning CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House
item.description: President Trump said Friday that he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, the latest move to target media outlets over their reporting.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 20)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Sampling some of the 40 essential dishes in Washington, D.C.
item.description: In August, the Washington Post ran an article called "The 40 essential dishes of D.C." Elazar Sontag and Tim Carman, who contributed to the piece, join "The Takeout" to sample some of the featured food.

item.title: Vance asks voters to give Republicans "another chance"
item.description: With the November midterms rapidly approaching, Vice President JD Vance is making a pitch to voters: "Give us another chance." New York Times congressional correspondent Annie Karni and Cook Political Report managing editor Carrie Dann join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: New book makes the case for how Democrats can build a lasting supermajority in Congress
item.description: It's hard for either party on Capitol Hill to function with a narrow majority. Democratic Party insider Adam Jentleson argues in his new book "Supermajority: How Democrats Can Build Lasting Power" that his party needs to draw from the past to get more congressional seats. Jentleson joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: The typically red Senate seats that are competitive this year
item.description: New data shows Democrats making inroads with voters in some red states holding Senate elections in November. Zachary Donnini, head of data science at VoteHub, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Pentagon releases UFO files with documents on secretive military program
item.description: The Pentagon on Friday released a new group of files about unidentified anomalous phenomena, or UAP or UFOs, including a batch of documents regarding a mysterious military program studying aerospace threats.

item.title: Watch: Pentagon releases 15 new UFO videos
item.description: The Defense Department released a sixth batch of UFO files on Friday, more than a month after its fifth drop. These are all of the videos in the latest tranche.

item.title: AI expected to loom large over Trump-Xi summit
item.description: President Trump is set to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., on Thursday amid mounting concerns about the safety of artificial intelligence. CBS News chief foreign affairs correspondent and "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan has more.

item.title: Will AI harm humans? Poll finds Americans want to slow development but not stop
item.description: Americans are optimistic about scientific advances in AI, but concerned that AI may take jobs.

item.title: Most Americans want to slow AI development but not stop it, CBS News poll finds
item.description: Will artificial intelligence harm humans? A new CBS News poll shows that most Americans find it likely. CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto breaks down the numbers.

item.title: Trump signs Russia sanctions bill championed by Graham
item.description: The new law lets the president impose tariffs on the largest purchases of Russian oil and natural gas.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addresses AI safety concerns: "2030 is not going to be the end of the world"
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has publicly come out against a coordinated slowdown between artificial intelligence companies in an interview with CBS News' Jo Ling Kent. Matt Shumer, author of the AI-focused newsletter "Something Big is Happening," joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he agrees with Trump on AI, doesn't believe it will end world by 2030
item.description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang tells CBS News' Jo Ling Kent he completely disagrees with the idea that AI will end up destroying the world by the end of the decade, saying there's a "0% chance" of that happening. Watch more from Kent's exclusive interview with Huang on "CBS Sunday Morning" September 20.

item.title: Major Garrett argues "Trump is signaling he's weak" with ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico
item.description: President Trump lashed out at reporters who cover his administration on Friday, saying he would ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. Major Garrett shares his thoughts on the ban and CBS News senior White House correspondent Weijia Jiang reports.

item.title: Trump says he's banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House
item.description: President Trump took questions from reporters on Friday after he said he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House. CBS News correspondent Natalie Brand and legal contributor Jessica Levinson have more.

item.title: 9/18: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: President Trump says he is banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House; Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang argues against artificial intelligence slowdown.

item.title: Mortgage rates are nearing 7%. One house hunter says he's "despondent."
item.description: "It seems like we're trying to climb out of a hole somebody else is digging," said one frustrated house hunter as homeownership costs rise.

item.title: Duncan Sheik, singer-songwriter of "Barely Breathing," dies at 56
item.description: Duncan Sheik died on Thursday night, his family said.

item.title: Twins conjoined at the head are separated in 25-hour surgery
item.description: The twins were born in Ethiopia with a rare condition that left them joined at the head. Doctors spent a year planning a separation surgery.

item.title: Sacramento Sikh truck driver survives being stabbed 17 times at Wyoming rest stop
item.description: A Sacramento Sikh truck driver was stabbed 17 times in an unprovoked attack at a Wyoming truck stop on Sunday, his attorney says.
